2608.19430.title: HARP: Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Preference-Adaptive Fusion for Query-Based CVE Prioritization
2608.19430.paper_summary: Vulnerability prioritization is inherently preference dependent, since the same CVE can receive different remediation priority under different operational preference scenarios. Existing scoring systems and ranking methods typically assume a fixed criterion. In practice, organizations already operate under a preference scenario, but this preference is often implicit and difficult to express as a written prompt instruction, while triage queries usually do not encode it. Past validated triage cases under the current scenario are more readily available. We study query-based CVE prioritization in this setting and propose HARP, a graph-grounded multi-view framework that ranks candidates from a natural-language query together with a support bank of historical labeled examples from the current preference scenario, without requiring an explicit textual summary of that scenario. HARP retrieves evidence from a vulnerability knowledge graph, scores candidates with policy-conditioned global, enterprise, and user views, and fits view-fusion weights from sampled supports. Experiments across three preference scenarios and multiple backbone LLMs show that HARP outperforms multiple baselines, expressing our method's effectiveness.
2608.19430.paper_summary_zh: 漏洞優先排序本質上依賴於偏好，因為相同的CVE在不同的操作偏好情境下可能會獲得不同的修復優先級。現有的評分系統和排名方法通常假設一個固定的標準。在實踐中，組織已經在一個偏好情境下運作，但這種偏好往往是隱含的，難以表達為書面提示指令，而分診查詢通常不會編碼它。在當前情境下，過去經過驗證的分診案例更容易獲得。我們在這種情境下研究基於查詢的CVE優先排序，並提出HARP，一個基於圖的多視角框架，該框架從自然語言查詢中排名候選者，並結合來自當前偏好情境的歷史標記示例的支持庫，而不需要該情境的明確文本摘要。HARP從漏洞知識圖中檢索證據，使用政策條件的全球、企業和用戶視角對候選者進行打分，並從抽樣支持中擬合視角融合權重。在三個偏好情境和多個骨幹LLM上的實驗顯示，HARP超越了多個基準，表現出我們方法的有效性。
